clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A nurse is reviewing the facility procedure for disposal of suctioned body fluids. Which statement is consistent with current CDC environmental-infection-control guidance?

options.A: Sanitary-sewer disposal may be used when local discharge requirements are met and the state accepts that method.
options.B: Sanitary-sewer disposal is permitted for every suction canister under one uniform national rule.
options.C: Every suction canister belongs in a sharps container even when the canister contains no sharps.
options.D: Suctioned body fluids may be discarded with ordinary solid waste regardless of jurisdictional requirements.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC's current summary recommendations state that sanitary sewers may be used for blood, suctioned fluids, ground tissues, excretions, and secretions provided that local sewage-discharge requirements are met and the state has declared the method acceptable. CDC's regulated-medical-waste guidance also notes that state regulations and local municipal restrictions can determine allowable methods or volumes. Therefore, there is no single universal disposal route for every suction canister; the nurse should follow the facility's approved process implementing applicable jurisdictional requirements.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Recognize that sanitary-sewer disposal of suctioned body fluids is acceptable only when state acceptance and local sewage-discharge requirements permit it.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Environmental Control Summary I.IV.E; Regulated Medical Waste §5
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, detailed printed p. 25
audit_findings_append.finding: The original item was directionally correct but structurally cued. The revised item makes the state/local qualification the tested concept and eliminates unsupported universal disposal assumptions.

option_audit.A: Correct. This states the two conditions CDC places on sanitary-sewer disposal of suctioned fluids.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. CDC explicitly conditions sewer disposal on state acceptance and local discharge requirements.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Sharps containers are for sharps; CDC does not direct every non-sharp suction-fluid container into a sharps container.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Jurisdictional regulated-medical-waste requirements cannot be disregarded.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone reproduces the CDC conditional recommendation without asserting a universal disposal method.
cueing_check: All four options are disposal-policy statements of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
